function: Learned delay-domain sparse precoder design (unrolled) jointly with CSIT and effective-CSIR estimation modules, trained end-to-end for BER to cut DMRS pilot overhead (p. 2, 7).
system: TDD MIMO-OFDM, Nt=Nr=8 and 16x16 antennas, K=1024 subcarriers, 80 MHz, 2.4 GHz indoor; no RIS (p. 12-13, Table I).
method: Deep unfolding (T=3) of the sparse EVM precoder with learned Lagrange multipliers, plus FC/1D-conv channel estimators; supervised end-to-end variational Bayesian training, pre-training then fine-tuning (p. 8-12).
data_channel: Simulated IEEE 802.11ax MIMO channel, delay profile model B, ray-tracing model of [45]; 10^5 random realizations for training, 10^4 for testing (p. 3, 12).
test_conditions: Trained on model B at random SNR per (L, B) setup; tested on model B and on model F, 10x larger RMS delay spread (p. 12, 15).
baselines: Non-learned: LS, OMP, VAMP, LASSO, genie MMSE, common precoder, sparse WMMSE; own ablations (proposed w/o DNN, EVM precoder with DNN-CE); no earlier learned method (p. 12-13).
metrics: BER (hard decision, 1024/4096-QAM), NMSE of CSIT and CSIR estimation, pilot overhead reduction (up to 8x), FLOPs, parameters, inference time (p. 13-15).
complexity: Table II: 438.0M FLOPs, 36.9M parameters, 17.14 ms inference in total (precoder module 329.5M FLOPs); Table III lists solution times (p. 13).
q1_support: p. 12: "802.11ax MIMO channel with the delay profile configured to model B" (IEEE 802.11ax model, not 3GPP; see notes).
q2_support: p. 15: "Despite being trained on model B, our proposed end-to-end DNN consistently achieves about 2 dB performance gain" under model F.
q3_support: p. 13: "we present the performance of two additional schemes alongside the proposed DNN solution for ablation studies". Missing: no earlier learned method; the other baselines (LS, OMP, VAMP, LASSO, Common, S-WMMSE) are non-learned.
q4_support: p. 13: "We summarize the parameter counts, FLOPs, and inference time on the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 in Table II."
q5_support: p. 12: "random channel realizations for training" are self-generated; no code or data link or release statement appears in the paper.
notes: Area 3 over 2: the method learns precoding and CSIT/CSIR estimation jointly, and the main metric is the end-to-end BER used as training loss (p. 2, 13-14). q1 marked 1 under the rule for another standardized model: IEEE 802.11ax (TGax) models B and F, cited as [54] on p. 12, with the ray-based formulation of [45] (p. 3); reviewer to confirm. Weights are trained per (L, B) setup, so the BER-vs-L sweep is not a q2 case.
